OLDAG.

This man gives his full name as Arthur William OLDAG, but is generally called "John" as a kind of nick name. He has accordingly published a book under the name "John OLDAY" (anglicising his surname) and has used this name for other purposes, but in the circumstances this can hardly be regarded as passing under an alias. He states that he was born in London on the 10th April 1905, that he is the illegitimate son of a German woman by a Scotchman, and that he lived as a child first in America and then in Germany. There is no confirmation of this story, but there seems little reason to question it, and he evidently satisfied the British Consul at Hamburg that he was entitled to a British passport in April 1937, the first occasion when he came to the notice of the British authorities.

Prior to this date he had lived for many years in Germany. He evidently has talents as a writer and cartoonist, and may have been reasonably successful as a journalist. He seems, however, to have lived a somewhat irregular life; he was imprisoned for dishonesty on one occasion; and according to his own book he has also been a drug addict and has practised as a faith healer. It may be that for purposes of publicity he has represented his life in Germany as wilder and therefore more romantic than it was. He admits that he was an opposition communist, which means that he was a communist in principle but opposed to the government of Stalin, but there is no reason to suppose he was prominent as a politician or closely connected with any Communist organization. No doubt he left Germany because life under the Nazi domination did not suit him.

In 1938 he was in London, where he lived first with one Rose FYLEMAN, an authoress who helped him with translating his book into English. Later he quarrelled with her and in September 1938 he married one Hilde MEISEL. This woman was described as a Hungarian subject born in Vienna, and appears to be of the usual type of intellectual international Jewess of Left-Wing tendencies. She has belonged for some years to the International League of Militant Socialists (often known as ISK), who are less violent than the name seems to imply.
